title: _mirror_api_input_caches calls path.endswith without the isinstance(path, str) guard its sibling validator uses — a non-string apiInput 'path' crashes the whole save with AttributeError
description: `_mirror_api_input_caches` does `path = cfg.get('path', '')` then `if not path.endswith(('.json', '.jsonl')):`. If `node.data.config['path']` is present but not a string (config is `dict[str, Any]`; the VALID_KEYS allowlist in `_config_io._prepare_config_for_sidecar` filters key *names*, not value *types*, so a `path` whose value is an int/list/dict survives to disk and back), the `.endswith` call raises `AttributeError`. That call sits OUTSIDE the per-node `try/except` (the try at line 626 only wraps `mirror_cache_to_committed`), so the AttributeError propagates up through `save()`'s try block, triggers `_rollback`, and re-raises as a 500. The sibling method `_validate_api_inputs_have_schemas` handles exactly this field defensively at line 579-580 (`path = cfg.get('path','') or ''` then `if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.endswith(...)`: continue), so the two methods that walk the same apiInput `path` field disagree on robustness. The mirror is a non-essential, explicitly idempotent best-effort promotion (its own docstring at 609-612 says partial state is fine and failures are merely logged), so a malformed non-string path aborting the entire save (including the code+config+sidecar writes that already succeeded) is the wrong failure mode.
evidence: _save_pipeline.py:620 `path = cfg.get('path', '')` (no `or ''`, no isinstance), :621 `if not path.endswith((".json", ".jsonl")):`. Contrast :579-580 in `_validate_api_inputs_have_schemas`: `path = cfg.get('path', '') or ''` then `if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.endswith((".json", ".jsonl")): continue`. The mirror try/except begins at :626 and wraps only `mirror_cache_to_committed(str(data_path))`, so a non-string `path` raises before it is reached.
